content: 1. Ritonavir increases the levels of desvenlafaxine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is involved in its metabolism. This interaction may lead to increased toxicity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 2. Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of deutetrabenazine by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6, which metabolizes the drug. Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors can increase systemic exposure to the active dihydro-metabolites of deutetrabenazine by approximately threefold. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 3. Lopinavir also increases the levels and effects of deutetrabenazine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors can similarly increase systemic exposure to the active dihydro-metabolites of deutetrabenazine by approximately threefold. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 4. Both lopinavir and deutetrabenazine can prolong the QTc interval. While deutetrabenazine at its maximum recommended dose does not clinically prolong the QT interval, certain conditions (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, co-administration with other QT-prolonging drugs, or congenital QT prolongation) may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Lopinavir increases the levels and effects of dexamethasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, ritonavir increases dexamethasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Conversely, dexamethasone decreases the levels and effects of ritonavir and lopinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. DHEA (herbal supplement) increases the levels and effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Ritonavir increases the levels of diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may lead to increased adverse effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Lopinavir similarly increases diazepam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Alternatives should be considered if available. 8. Lopinavir decreases the levels of diazepam buccal by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism, while ritonavir increases diazepam buccal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 9. Lopinavir decreases the levels of diazepam intranasal by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism, while ritonavir increases diazepam intranasal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Lopinavir increases the effects of diazoxide, potentially through mechanisms not fully understood. Ritonavir similarly increases diazoxide effects. Reports suggest hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Lopinavir and ritonavir decrease the levels of didanosine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. Both drugs also increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome when co-administered. Caution is necessary. 12. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels and effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in plasma levels of estrogen and progestin have been observed with HIV protease inhibitors, potentially leading to adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. Monitoring is recommended. 13. Ritonavir increases the levels of digoxin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and by reducing renal and hepatic clearance. Plasma concentrations and pharmacologic effects of digoxin may be elevated, increasing the risk of toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Diltiazem increases the levels and effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, ritonavir increases diltiazem levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 15. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels and effects of docetaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir also affects the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 16. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels of dofetilide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may lead to increased toxicity. Therapy modification, close monitoring, and consideration of alternatives are advised due to the risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. 17. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels and effects of doravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Ritonavir increases the levels of doxepin by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels and effects of dronabinol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 20. Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of doxorubicin and doxorubicin liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Dronedarone increases the levels and effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Ritonavir increases the levels of duloxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 23. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels and effects of duvelisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases duvelisib AUC, raising the risk of toxicities. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 24. Ritonavir and efavirenz both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Efavirenz decreases the levels of lopinavir and ritonavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 25. Elagolix increases the levels of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter but decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Therapy modification and monitoring are recommended. 26. Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of eletriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels of eluxadoline by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, caution is advised when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 28. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels and effects of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 29. Ritonavir and emtricitabine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Encorafenib inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 31. Ritonavir increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Enfortumab vedotin releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), which is metabolized by CYP3A4. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase MMAE exposure, raising the risk of toxicities. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Ritonavir and enfuvirtide both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 33. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels of escitalopram by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing the risk of serotonin syndrome and toxicity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Ritonavir increases the levels and effects of erlotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) increases the levels of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary.
